correctness.rationale: The coefficient moment v_n is computed exactly by twice differentiating a finite beta-product. The diagonal unitary model is explicit. The error from its triangular asymptotic matrix is Hilbert--Schmidt: the n>=m summands are dominated by three independently summable series and the m>n/low-index regions are square summable. Schur testing with 1/sqrt(n log n) bounds the tail matrix norm by 2+1/(N log N). Explicit weakly-null finitely supported vectors indexed by logarithmic scales give a lower bound tending to 2. Boundedness, quantifiers and area/weight normalization are verified; finite checker outputs are not treated as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The new statement assigns an exact numerical essential norm to the critical asymmetric map. The September 2026 primary source proves endpoint boundedness only; the 2022 exact essential-norm theorem assumes the same function space as both domain and codomain and therefore cannot specialize to this map. The 2023 near-title comparison concerns bounds above the critical exponent, not the endpoint. Targeted searches returned no matching quantitative theorem. An uninspected related 2026 publication and unindexed equivalents remain residual risks, not evidence of non-overlap.

value.rationale: The newly established bounded but noncompact critical logarithmic endpoint has an intrinsically motivated unknown invariant: the best possible compact and finite-rank approximation error. Identifying its exact value 2 quantitatively resolves that endpoint obstruction, via a structural Hilbert--Schmidt/Copson reduction, and improves the binary compactness classification. It is not a routine scalar replacement, a finite numerical sample, or a special-case substitution of the 2022 same-space theorem.
